title: Wandering is the activity.
summary: Inside the Book Barn in Niantic, Connecticut: room to wander, browse and take your time, with real outing observations and useful visit notes.
search: The Book Barn, Niantic · from our family camera roll.The Book Barn · a family field noteWandering is the activity.Books, gardens and curious corners. An afternoon without a prescribed route. Come alongA bookstore with room around it.The Book Barn feels like someone forgot to put walls around a bookstore. Books outside, books inside, gardens and odd corners. Our plan leaves space for wandering and one promising shelf.Looking for practical details? From our family notebook · NianticA bookstore without a script.The Book Barn is technically a used bookstore, but that description is as incomplete as calling the Maine coast “some water.” It is books, yes, but also paths, porches, garden corners, little buildings, signs, animals and the gentle feeling that the rules of an ordinary shop have loosened their tie.That is what we love about it. You do not enter and immediately feel the pressure of a proper cultural outing. There is no single route through the experience, no exhibit you are supposed to appreciate in the correct order. Someone can browse mysteries. Someone else can stay outside. You can look at three shelves or thirty. The wandering is the activity.From the existing family notebook. The photograph is our own; the decorative illustrations are interpretations, not current venue photographs.A subject that catches your eye is a good place to begin.From the rest of our notebook +On our visit, the place felt almost designed for a family that does better when the day contains choices but not demands. We could move. We could separate and come back together. We could notice whatever caught our attention instead of trying to maintain one shared pace. The atmosphere did much of the work for us: old books, greenery, bits of shade, curious corners, that slightly eccentric New England conviction that a perfectly reasonable business can sprawl across a property like a village.It is also the sort of place that gives a camera roll some texture: not a row of posed smiles, but hands on book spines, a path disappearing around a corner, a funny sign, someone absorbed in something that caught their eye. Those are the photographs we tend to keep. They look like the day felt—interesting, a little untidy, and entirely our own. Books and animals belong to the story. This cat is an illustration.The find is part of itOne promising shelf.And used bookstores have another advantage: they make very small victories feel satisfying. You do not need a major purchase. Finding one strange title, one old cookbook, one book about a topic somebody loves—that is enough. The object becomes a souvenir without announcing itself as one.Browse. Wander. Step outside. Leave when you are ready.What stays with us is the feeling of permission. Browse. Wander. Step outside. Look at something else. Come back. Leave when you are ready. It is a place with texture rather than a schedule, and that makes it one of those rare stops where the grown-ups can genuinely enjoy themselves without needing everybody to enjoy it in exactly the same way.Family story retained from our earlier notes, memory and camera roll. title: A conference, a castle, and a very convenient pool.
summary: A Gaylord Palms Fiber Connect conference, Disney’s Pop Century stay, a Skyliner ride and a Crystal Palace meal—with original photos and practical Orlando travel notes.
search: The journal/Travel · Orlando, Florida Fiber Connect, with the Graphical Networks team.A working trip, with a little room for wonderA conference, a castle, and a very convenient pool.Fiber Connect brought me to Florida. Staying at Disney gave the hours around work a little extra charm.Published October 6, 2026 Work: Fiber ConnectStay: Pop CenturyFlight: JetBlueMap & placesPractical tipsPrint a planning list There are work trips where the hotel is simply where you leave your suitcase. On this one, I stayed at Disney’s Pop Century Resort—and the pool was right outside my room.An excellent detail. Possibly the detail I should lead with.I flew JetBlue to Florida for Fiber Connect with Graphical Networks. The conference took place at the beautiful Gaylord Palms Resort & Convention Center, while Pop Century was my home base. Around the work came a lovely Skyliner ride, the Crystal Palace buffet, and a little time at Disney.I’m a longtime fan of Funspot in New Hampshire and the documentary The King of Kong: A Fistful of Quarters.Michael and James stayed home. The Evil Queen, however, made an appearance. ;) A little Magic Kingdom time around the work schedule.A Disney address for a working tripThe pleasure of being close.Gaylord Palms was a lovely setting for the conference. Staying at Pop Century gave the trip another atmosphere altogether: bright, playful, and unmistakably Disney.And then there was that pool. Having it right outside my room was such a pleasure. After a day of work, I appreciated being close to something enjoyable without having to organize another outing.Even when James isn’t traveling with me, I notice those practical details.
